public_rationale: PitchBook/NVCA reports that US venture funds raised $108.5 billion from January through September 2026 [e1]. This measures fundraising commitments, not remaining deployable capital [e1]. The interim figures neither establish system-wide exhaustion nor rule out exhaustion before the forecast deadline [e1].
limitations: The evidence does not provide a complete balance of deployable capital, including callable commitments, deployment and replenishment [e1].
The data end on September 30, 2026 and cannot settle the June 8, 2027 deadline outcome [e1].

our_interpretation: Assess the screened forecast about exhaustion of US venture capital, rather than issuing separate verdicts on every contextual clause.
The ordinary reading is system-wide exhaustion of available investment capital, not merely difficult fundraising for some managers.
Available investment capital means deployable fund capital, including callable commitments and replenishment through fundraising.
Eighteen months from December 8, 2025 ends on June 8, 2027.
The statements about AI-company financing and the PIF provide context; the forecast does not expressly make their continuation an antecedent.
Infinite is rhetorical and supplies no measurable funding amount.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable system-wide records establish exhaustion of deployable US venture-fund capital within the forecast interval.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At the deadline, material deployable capital remains and records show no earlier system-wide exhaustion during the interval.
